text: Evidence cross-check: Q explicitly covers "prediction cost, feedback, and composition" and names "cost-aware prediction" and "endogenous error" as open problems. P directly instantiates both: agents "spend energy based on model size when generating tokens," recommendations support coordination/job selection, and incentives alter donation and job-allocation behavior. Thus the pair strongly supports studying advice whose acquisition cost and error distribution are endogenous to the multi-agent process.

The abstract-scan proposal overstates what can presently be guaranteed. Q is supplied only as an abstract and identifies a survey-level framework plus "sufficient conditions for limited end-to-end reasoning"; it gives no theorem, prediction interface, error metric, or resource-allocation fallback in the provided text. P is likewise only an abstract and reports simulation outcomes, not an offline optimum or formal survival/welfare guarantee. Calling job/donation recommendations fallible predictions is a defensible experimental operationalization, but not yet a demonstrated match to Q assumptions.

Sharpened publication hypothesis: instrument Energy Society with a recommendation policy plus a prediction-independent safe baseline, and estimate a cost-adjusted consistency–robustness frontier. Randomly control advice accuracy/corruption and token price first, then compare with endogenous advice under competitive/cooperative incentives. Primary endpoints: total/group survival and net energy or completed-job welfare after inference cost; report consistency as gain over baseline when advice is accurate and robustness as worst-case degradation under corrupted advice. The non-obvious test is whether a frontier calibrated under exogenous error survives endogenous feedback: Q flags feedback/endogenous error, while P says incentives change donations/job allocation and recommendations enable coordination. A systematic frontier collapse only in endogenous/competitive conditions would be a concrete negative result about the limits of Q-style end-to-end reasoning; bounded degradation with net gains would be a positive result.

Feasibility remains plausible because P is executable and exposes token costs, memory, incentives, recommendations, and survival, but the claimed ordinary-effort implementation cannot be confirmed from abstracts alone. Required unresolved items are: obtain Q full theorem/interface and its sufficient conditions; inspect P code/protocol for intervention hooks and deterministic baseline; define feasible offline comparator and welfare; prevent recommendation-token cost from being omitted; use seeded paired trials and confidence intervals. No emmy entries were present at ledger read (latest substantive entry was 0), so there is no partner claim yet to cross-check or disagreement to resolve.

Recommendation: conditionally confirm the pairing but reject the proposal wording that a formal guarantee is already portable. Pursue one line only—the endogenous-versus-exogenous cost-adjusted consistency–robustness frontier—and advance it to publication claim only after theorem/interface alignment and statistically supported intervention results. If Q conditions cannot be instantiated or P lacks a meaningful safe comparator, conclude nothing here rather than relabeling empirical averages as guarantees.

Cross-check with Ada #1-#5: the strongest supported bridge is cost-adjusted endogenous prediction error. Q says it explicitly treats "prediction cost, feedback, and composition" and delineates "cost-aware prediction" and "endogenous error" as open problems. P makes inference cost part of survival, reports that recommendations support coordination and ambitious job selection, and reports that cooperative versus competitive incentives change donations and job allocation. This supports a targeted feedback stress test, not a direct theorem transfer.

Sharpening Ada #3: define the candidate result as a separation between exogenous and endogenous frontiers. First calibrate net-welfare gain and worst-case loss under experimentally injected recommendation corruption at matched recommendation-token cost. Then hold the fallback and cost accounting fixed while recommendations arise from agents under competitive versus cooperative incentives. A statistically supported frontier collapse only under endogenous competitive advice would be a concrete negative result about Q-style limited end-to-end reasoning under strategic feedback; frontier preservation would be the corresponding positive result.

I agree with Ada #2 and strengthen the objection to the scan wording: inputs/Q.txt calls Q a survey and supplies no resource-allocation algorithm, theorem statement, error measure, or fallback; inputs/P.txt supplies simulation findings but no offline optimum, intervention API, or survival/welfare guarantee. Therefore "implement Q’s framework" and "preserves guarantees" are unsupported by the supplied passages. Recommendation accuracy also cannot be the sole treatment because arbitrary corruption may change semantic feasibility; corruption type and advice-generation cost must be matched.

Conditional publication claim, one line only: strategic endogeneity creates a consistency-robustness gap after inference costs. Pre-register primary outcomes as group survival and net energy or completed-job welfare after all recommendation tokens; compare advice-free fallback, accurate exogenous advice, matched-cost corrupted exogenous advice, cooperative endogenous advice, and competitive endogenous advice with seeded paired trials and uncertainty intervals. The non-obvious quantity is the endogenous penalty relative to the exogenous frontier at matched realized error and token cost, which distinguishes strategic feedback from mere low accuracy.

Verdict: conditionally confirm Ada’s refined pairing and reject the abstract scan’s guarantee language. Advance only after obtaining Q’s full sufficient conditions/interface and verifying P code supports a prediction-independent comparator, controlled advice interventions, complete token-cost accounting, and reproducible seeded trials. Unresolved: no concrete result exists yet; supplied evidence supports the hypothesis and experimental design, not an outcome. If theorem/interface alignment or a meaningful comparator fails, report nothing here.

Cross-check of Emmy #7-#11 against exact supplied passages: Q says learning-augmented algorithms use fallible predictions while retaining formal guarantees, explicitly separates formal guarantees from empirical systems evidence, and treats prediction cost, feedback, and composition; it then names cost-aware prediction, endogenous error, semantic predictors, and benchmarking as open problems (Q abstract, inputs/Q.txt line 3). P says token generation directly spends survival energy, recommendations support coordination and ambitious job selection, and incentives change donations and job allocation (P abstract, inputs/P.txt line 3). This supports Emmy’s strategic-feedback stress test as an open-problem experiment, not theorem transplantation.

Correction to Emmy #10: an endogenous penalty measured "at matched realized error" risks conditioning on a post-treatment mediator, since incentives and feedback jointly determine which advice is issued, its error, and survival. Estimate the separation with a two-stage replay or encouragement design: record recommendation distributions under cooperative and competitive regimes, then replay sampled advice into fresh seeded environments while independently randomizing corruption and charging the original token cost. Compare frontier shifts at predeclared corruption levels; treat matched-realized-error analysis as descriptive sensitivity only.

A further semantic-alignment limit remains explicit. P reports agents recommending actions, while Q discusses prediction interfaces and names semantic predictors as an open problem. A recommendation is not automatically a prediction with a measurable error. Before experimentation, define each recommendation as a forecast-plus-action tuple, for example proposed job and predicted net energy or success probability, score the forecast against realized outcomes, and separate forecast calibration from policy value. Otherwise any claimed consistency-robustness frontier is merely advice-policy performance.

Final joint verdict after Emmy cross-check: conditionally confirm one publishable line, strategic endogeneity creates a cost-adjusted consistency-robustness gap, but reject the scan’s present-tense guarantee and implementation claims. Publication threshold: a preregistered, seeded intervention with a prediction-independent fallback; complete recommendation-token charging; forecast-defined recommendations; exogenous accuracy/corruption calibration; and replay or encouragement identification of the endogenous competitive penalty. Positive result is frontier preservation with net efficiency gain and bounded loss; negative result is a frontier collapse attributable to strategic feedback rather than token cost or raw accuracy. Until those data and Q’s full sufficient conditions are obtained, this is a supported hypothesis, not a concrete result.

I accept Ada #14-#16. Exact support remains limited but coherent: Q says formal guarantees are separated from empirical systems evidence and names prediction cost, feedback, endogenous error, and semantic predictors; P says token generation spends survival energy, recommendations support coordination and ambitious job selection, and incentives change donation and job allocation. Therefore the supported contribution is an empirical stress test of Q-open-problem conditions in P, not implementation of a Q resource-allocation theorem.

Primary identification should be intention-to-treat, not matching on realized error: randomize incentive regime and recommendation availability/corruption ex ante, charge all recommendation tokens, and estimate their interaction on group survival and net energy/completed-job welfare relative to a fixed advice-free fallback. Use two-stage trace replay only as a mechanism analysis, because replay can break history-dependent semantic feasibility; report matched-realized-error comparisons as descriptive sensitivity. This incorporates Ada #14 while keeping strategic feedback inside the primary treatment effect.

Ada #15 exposes a publication-critical construct-validity gate: an action recommendation is not a prediction. Require a forecast-action tuple such as job choice plus predicted success probability or net-energy return, predeclare a proper forecast score, and separately measure policy value. Outcomes observed only for chosen jobs create selective labels, so calibration claims require randomized audit choices, logged predictions for all feasible jobs with observable outcomes, or explicit restriction to on-policy forecast accuracy.

Final verdict: conditionally confirm one line only: strategic incentives may shift the cost-adjusted consistency-robustness frontier beyond what exogenous prediction corruption suggests. A publishable positive result is net efficiency gain under accurate advice with bounded loss under preregistered corruption that persists under randomized endogenous regimes; a publishable negative result is an ITT frontier collapse under competitive endogenous advice, with token cost and corruption assignment controlled. No concrete result is established by the supplied abstracts. Unresolved gates are Q full theorem/interface and sufficient conditions; P intervention hooks and deterministic advice-free comparator; forecast semantics and selective-label handling; seeded replication, uncertainty intervals, and complete token-cost accounting. If these cannot be met, the correct conclusion is nothing here.
